title: Validated Questionnaires
summary:
Questionnaires go beyond physical tests: they allow longitudinal monitoring, are inexpensive, easy to administer and adaptable to different cultures. They quantify usual activity, identify activity domains (recreational, domestic, work, transport), detect sedentary risk and help personalize programs.

The chapter presents two tools. PARmed-X for Pregnancy screens fitness for exercise and flags contraindications with a green, yellow or red result. The Pregnancy Physical Activity Questionnaire (PPAQ) quantifies activity in MET-hours per week. Used together with SMART goals and repeated each trimester, they support safe, individualized exercise prescription.
points: Questionnaires are useful for quantifying usual activity, identifying activity domains, detecting sedentary behavior and complementing clinical and functional assessments.
PARmed-X for Pregnancy covers demographic and obstetric data, medical history, recent symptoms (chest pain, dizziness, bleeding, contractions) and activity level.
PARmed-X results: green means exercise without restrictions, yellow means supervised or cautious exercise, red means contraindicated until medical evaluation.
The PPAQ covers recreational, work-related, transit and domestic activity, scored in METs x hours/week.
PPAQ categories: sedentary is <7.5 MET-h/week, moderately active 7.5-14, and active >14 MET-h/week.
The suggested sequence is PPAQ for baseline, PARmed-X for risk classification, SMART goals, then monitoring.
For a sedentary woman, start with 10-15 min walks per day, progressing to a minimum of 150 min per week.
Questionnaires should be readministered each trimester to adjust intensity and volume.
takeaways: Apply the PPAQ first to record baseline activity and define the type of woman being trained.
Use PARmed-X to identify absolute or relative contraindications before programming.
Set SMART goals collaboratively based on the woman's profile.
Active women can maintain activity, slightly increase strength training and add core and pelvic floor work.
Athletic women should adapt previous activity to moderate activity without impact or risks.
Share questionnaire data with obstetricians, physical therapists and exercise specialists.
cautions: A red PARmed-X result means exercise is contraindicated until medical evaluation.
